subject: Literature
title: Thomas Paine's Common Sense
description: One-minute skill: Thomas Paine's Common Sense.

hook.text: A forty-seven-page pamphlet written by a failed corset-maker convinced an entire continent to declare independence.

buildup.text: Thomas Paine's Common Sense sold over five hundred thousand copies in 1776, reaching nearly every American colonist.

discovery.text: Paine argued in plain language that monarchy was absurd and that America should govern itself. The effect was electric.

twist.text: Britain banned the pamphlet and charged Paine with sedition, but by then the Revolution was already unstoppable.

climax.text: Common Sense proved that a banned book can be more dangerous to a government than an army on a battlefield.

punchline.text: One pamphlet outfought the entire British Empire.

quiz.question: What impact did Common Sense have on the American Revolution?
options: It had very little effect on public opinion
It convinced colonists in plain language that independence was necessary
It was only read by military leaders, not ordinary people
